source: ប្រភេទស្មៅដែលដុះក្នុងស្រែ (Types of Weeds Growing in Rice Fields), agrochemical product-training slide deck for the Hai Au Agro brand herbicides 'Hai Au YOYO 300EC' (Pretilachlor 300g/L + Fenclorim 100g/L) and 'Hai Au Alo 200EC' (Cyhalofop-butyl 200g/L); no institutional letterhead, presenter name, or date visible anywhere in the deck
text: Weeds compete with rice for water, nutrients, and space, and left uncontrolled they can reduce rice yield by roughly 40-50%. Weeds also host insect pests and diseases that then spread to the rice crop, harbor pest-carrying vectors, and increase the labor and cost needed for weeding. The source shows common weed types found in rice fields (narrow-leaf grasses, sedges, and broadleaf weeds growing among rice) without naming every species individually, and frames the central question 'how can rice avoid competing with weeds?' by pointing to timely and complete weed control as the key lesson, comparing an untreated plot choked with weeds against a properly-weeded plot with clean, vigorous rice stands.
